traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report contains two nested studies (initial validation with two-dilution interpretation, Section 3, and an extension study with single-dilution/single-plate interpretation, Section 4), each further split by reference-method incubation temperature (30°C in Table 21-right / Section 3 tables, and 37°C in Table 21-left). I selected the 'Two dilutions' (initial validation) relative trueness results at 37°C incubation of the reference method (right-hand columns of Table 21, page 13) as the canonical/primary per-category dataset, since this corresponds to the main methods-comparison relative trueness study described in Section 3.1. The 30°C version (Table 20) and the single-plate/extension-study versions (left-hand columns of both Table 20 and Table 21) contain very similar but not identical bias/SD/n/CI values per category and are not included here to avoid duplicating categories; they are structurally parallel (same category list) but reflect the alternative single-dilution protocol and/or 30°C reference incubation rather than the primary two-dilution/37°C study. Note that Table 21 (two-dilution, 37°C) does not include a 'Dairy & egg products' row (that category appears only in Table 20 at 30°C, with n=25, SD=-0.07, Bias=0.13, LCL=-0.34, UCL=0.20) -- I left its quantitative fields null here since it was not present in the specific canonical table chosen, to avoid mixing data from different sub-studies; this should be treated as a gap rather than a true zero/absence of testing. All 'All cat.' / 'Total' aggregate rows from Tables 20 and 21 were excluded per instructions. Acceptability limit of ±0.5 log10 CFU/g or mL is explicitly stated in Sections 3.2.1 and 4.2.1.
